title: 2026 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia
extractionNote: Selected summaries of sections 2.1 and 4.2.6 and Table 1, focused on secondary ASCVD prevention. This is not the complete guideline; consult the source for individual recommendation wording and COR/LOE. Confirm the full ASCVD risk category before selecting a treatment goal.

recommendations.text: Very-high-risk ASCVD requires ≥2 major ASCVD events, or 1 major event plus ≥2 high-risk features. Ischemic stroke counts as a major event. High-risk features include age ≥65, coronary bypass/PCI, current smoking, diabetes, heart failure, hypertension, or LDL-C ≥100 mg/dL despite maximally tolerated statin plus ezetimibe.

recommendations.section: 4.2.6. Secondary ASCVD Prevention; Table 1 — not at very high risk
recommendations.text: For adults with clinical ASCVD not at very high risk, use high-intensity statin therapy targeting ≥50% LDL-C reduction, LDL-C <70 mg/dL and non-HDL-C <100 mg/dL.

recommendations.section: 4.2.6. Secondary ASCVD Prevention; Table 1 — at very high risk
recommendations.text: For very-high-risk ASCVD, target LDL-C <55 mg/dL and non-HDL-C <85 mg/dL. Add ezetimibe and/or a PCSK9 monoclonal antibody to maximally tolerated statin therapy according to the reduction needed and patient preference.

recommendations.section: 4.2.6. Secondary ASCVD Prevention; Table 1 — additional lowering
recommendations.text: For ASCVD not at very high risk, further lowering toward LDL-C <55 mg/dL and non-HDL-C <85 mg/dL with ezetimibe, a PCSK9 monoclonal antibody or bempedoic acid can also be reasonable on maximally tolerated statin therapy after considering treatment needs and preferences.
